intro.text:
You walked out of the Crater. People don't, usually.

I'm Ilse Marrow. I keep the hearth-page of Lanternfast, and the hearth keeps us. Whatever you are, you're welcome to the warmth — but not the water. Our well's gone black.

options.text: The ash in the Crater fell upward. Does that happen often?
The ash in the Crater fell upward. Does that happen often?

well.text:
Three days ago the water came up thick and dark and moving. Living ink — the kind that crawls off torn pages. Our well is fed by a channel from the spring in the Drowned Orchard, east past the ridge.

I sent Tamsin, my runner. She hasn't come back.

options.text: I'll find out what's fouling the spring.

reward.text: Honest, at least. I have a warden's hook that has burned three hounds to cinders, and Tamsin's knife — if it comes to that. Clean water, and one of them is yours.

accept.text:
Thank you. Take the road south and east, through the gap in the ridge. The orchard lives under the Edict of Kindling — anything there burns twice as hot. Mind the oil seeps. Use them, if you're clever.

And if you find Tamsin... bring her home. One way or another.

place.text:
Lanternfast. Forty souls and a page of the Ledger nailed above the hearth. It says warmth is owed to all who shelter here, and the world still listens: wounds close, and the hounds can't follow you through the gate.

Outside our walls, every law is somebody else's.

crater_ok.text:
You noticed. Most don't — they're too busy being grateful to be alive.

The Crater holds a page that remembers the sky. The old scribes said places like that are where the Ledger is trying to put itself back together. Don't tell Brother Cale I said so. He'd make a hymn of it.

crater_fail.text: Ash does what ash likes. That's the whole trouble with the world.

progress.text: The spring. East, through the ridge. Tamsin went that way.

variants.text: You've learned something out there; I can see it on you. Ink burns, doesn't it? Then burn it clean, if you can.

options.text: I found Tamsin. The hounds got to her first.

early_report.text: You've been to the spring already, haven't you? Something's changed in the well. Tell me.

options.text: Let me tell you what happened.

variants.text: The water's coming up grey instead of black. Grey I can boil. You killed it, didn't you — whatever was in the spring.
The water is... clear. Clear. I haven't seen it clear since I was a girl. What did you do?
The well is singing. Do you hear it? It's singing, and the children won't stop listening to it. What did you DO out there?

options.text: I found Tamsin. The hounds got to her first.
A bloated leech-mother was feeding the ink. She's dead.
I burned the ink out of the spring. The mother fled into the deep.
Brother Cale asked me to finish the Choir's rite. I did.
The ink is gone. Nothing was ever wrong.

tamsin_told.text:
...Then she found it before I did. She always did run ahead.

Thank you for telling me. Most wouldn't have bothered.

reward_choice.text: Then I keep my word. Take your pick.

options.text: The Lanternhook. (Fire hook: heavy attacks ignite what they strike.)
Tamsin's quiet knife. (Fast knife: backstabs, steam on dodge.)
I'll take both. I earned them.

both_ok.text: ...Ha. Fine. Fine! Take both and get out of my sight before I change my mind.

both_fail.text: No. Pick one, or pick none.

thanks.text: Lanternfast won't forget this. Neither will I. If you're looking for trouble, the Hush lies west — the old graveyard. Nothing there stays dead. Don't go until you're ready.

choir_end.text:
Get out.

...No. Stay. You're the only one who came back. But don't ever ask me for anything again.

lie_ok.text:
...Nothing wrong. Yes. Yes, you're right. Listen to it — it's almost beautiful. Thank you, stranger.

(She believes you. You are not sure that is better.)

lie_fail.text: Don't. I've buried enough liars to know the look. The Choir got to you.

variants.text: The children are drinking from the well again. That's your doing, stranger. Lanternfast remembers.
The well sings at night. I've stopped sleeping.

options.text: The bell in the Hush has stopped.
What lies behind the sealed door in the orchard cliffs?
I've read about the night the Ledger burned. The Scribes lit the fire themselves.

scriptorium.text:
The Scriptorium. Where the Ledger was kept. Ink seals it now, and they say the lock wants a name — the name of whoever struck the match. Nobody living knows it.

You look at me like you might.

burning.text:
The Scribes? On purpose?

...My grandmother said the fire started in the Scriptorium and walked out of it on two legs. I thought it was a story for frightening children.

hush_told.text:
I heard. Half the town came out to listen to the quiet.

Take these marks. It isn't much, but it's what we have.

variants.text:
You read them? All of them? My grandmother's sister is in that book.

Take these marks. It isn't much, but it's what we have.
